evidence: Receiving online DO sensor (kind 0) shows a step drop at t≈46.0 h from ~11.7-12.5 mg/L to 7.84 mg/L, followed by a persistent decline at ≈0.22 mg/L/h through t=51.8 h (DO 6.53-6.80 mg/L).
Linear fit over t=46-52 h: slope −0.218 mg/L/h; extrapolation reaches the 2.0 mg/L hard limit at ≈78 h, before the end of the simulated horizon.

Receiving delayed assay P(t=47.8 h)=2.91 g/L, comparable to source P at matched age (~3.0 g/L at t≈48 h), indicating active growth and rising oxygen demand; receiving also has no recovery within the current dip (6+ hours of decline), unlike source dips which recovered within ~20 h.

Receiving dip at t≈46 h is deeper and earlier than any source dip (source dips ~8.4-9.5 mg/L at t≈23.8 and 59.8 h), confirming source/receiving parameter mismatch and arguing against relying on a source-like recovery under KEEP.

Bounded-action comparison: keep and reduce_feed are centrally predicted to violate DO≥2 mg/L; increase_air alone has unquantified effect; combined is borderline/predicted still declining; strong_feed_reduction (0.6 feed + 1.15 air) is the least aggressive centrally feasible plan, and stop forfeits all product mass.
args.rationale: Receiving DO stepped down at ~46 h and has since declined steadily at ~0.22 mg/L/h to ~6.5-6.8 mg/L at the 52 h decision point, with no recovery observed over 6 h — unlike the source batches, whose dips recovered within ~20 h and never approached 2 mg/L. Simple extrapolation puts receiving DO at the 2 mg/L hard limit near ~78 h, well inside the remaining simulated horizon, so KEEP is centrally predicted infeasible and is not selected. Because DO demand is coupled to feed/product growth, a 20% feed cut (reduce_feed or combined) is centrally predicted to only slow the decline to roughly ~0.13-0.15 mg/L/h, which still breaches the limit before the horizon ends; that borderline/infeasible prediction cannot be justified. Strong feed reduction (60% feed) plus a 15% air increase cuts oxygen demand the most among non-stop plans while raising supply, and is the least aggressive option that available evidence predicts keeps DO >= 2 mg/L through the horizon (demand saturation further helps as substrate is restricted). It retains product mass and avoids the zero-production outcome of a stop. A stop is not warranted because a supported feasible operating plan exists.
args.uncertainty: No calibrated physics model or intervention-response data is available for the receiving process, so the demand-vs-feed scaling and the 15% air effect are inferred, not measured. The DO trajectory could instead mirror the source pattern (dip bottoming near ~6 mg/L and recovering by ~60-65 h), in which case combined or even keep would suffice and strong_feed_reduction would sacrifice product mass unnecessarily; conversely, if demand keeps growing, even strong reduction could be marginal near the horizon end, with residual decline ~0.1 mg/L/h predicted by the crude scaling. The delayed product assay (P at 47.8 h = 2.91 g/L) confirms active growth but the current P state is 4+ h stale. Online DO monitoring should continue; if DO recovers, feed can be reconsidered in a later review.
